# Standard: sitemap links on the primary domain over https

The baseline for every Drupal site we maintain: each `<loc>` in the live sitemap starts with
`https://` and the **primary domain**, the host Pantheon serves without redirecting.

**Why:** the sitemap is generated by cron from the CLI, where there is no request to take the
scheme or host from, so the module falls back to a stored base URL. Left alone, that base is
whatever someone typed years ago (often `http://`, or `www` when the primary is now the bare
domain), or empty, which gives `http://default`. Every link then answers with a redirect. A
sitemap is meant to list canonical URLs; Google reports each redirecting entry as "Page with
redirect" and gives it little weight, so the sitemap stops telling search engines which URLs
are the real ones. On wac (2026-10-26) all 667 links were `https://www.isd110.org` while Pantheon's
primary-domain policy 301s `www` to `isd110.org`. Kaza had seen plenty of sites shipping
`http` sitemaps and made it a check for every site.

**Check** against live, since local generates from local state:

```bash
curl -s https://<primary>/sitemap.xml | grep -oE '<loc>[a-z]+://[^/<]+' | sort | uniq -c
curl -sI https://<a-loc-host>/ | grep -iE '^(HTTP|location|x-pantheon-redirect)'
```

One line of output, `https://<primary>`, and that host answering 200 rather than 301. For a
sitemap index, check a child sitemap too.

**Apply** on live only, in code. Settings outrank state and config, and other environments
should keep building links on their own host:

```php
// settings.php — xmlsitemap (otherwise read from state xmlsitemap_base_url).
if (($_ENV['PANTHEON_ENVIRONMENT'] ?? '') === 'live') {
  $settings['xmlsitemap_base_url'] = 'https://<primary>';
}
// settings.php — simple_sitemap (otherwise config simple_sitemap.settings:base_url).
if (($_ENV['PANTHEON_ENVIRONMENT'] ?? '') === 'live') {
  $config['simple_sitemap.settings']['base_url'] = 'https://<primary>';
}
```

Verify locally by putting the same line in `settings.local.php`, regenerating
(`drush xmlsitemap:regenerate` or `drush simple-sitemap:generate`) and re-running the check
on the ddev URL, then take it back out. Live picks the change up at its next regeneration,
or regenerate after the deploy. The `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt should name the same URL
([[pantheon-robots-txt]]).
